Theme

Work & responsibility

secretary noun

someone who writes letters and keeps records for another

also secretaries, personal assistant, PA, clerk, amanuensis, recording secretary

classical

Cic. Att. 12.40.1: librum ut tuīs librāriīs daret (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 180

librārius, librāriī m.

noun, second declension

a private secretary, a clerk

Lewis & Short (s.v. scrība): librārius is the private secretary, scrība the public one. Its first sense is a copyist of books, and after Augustus also a bookseller, so the setting must show which is meant.

Other words

  • ā manū (servus) — a secretary, one who writes for his master

    also used · classical · Suet. Caes. 74: ā manū servus (Lewis & Short, s.v. ab); Traupman 169

    The household slave who wrote at his master’s dictation; ā manū esse, to be someone’s secretary. Traupman gives it for a secretary, with āmanuēnsis.

  • āmanuēnsis, āmanuēnsis m. — a clerk, a secretary

    noun, third declension · also used · post-classical · Suet. Tib. 3; Ner. 44 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 169

    Only in Suetonius (Lewis & Short), made from ā manū; the source of English amanuensis.

  • scrība, scrībae m. — a public clerk, a clerk to a magistrate

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.3.183 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 292

    The salaried clerk of the Roman magistrates, who kept the public accounts and records (Lewis & Short): the word for the secretary of a council, a court or a society. In Christian Latin, a scribe of the Jewish law.

  • notārius, notāriī m. — a shorthand writer; a secretary who takes dictation

    noun, second declension · also used · post-classical · Plin. Ep. 9.36.2 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. secretary

  • ab epistulīs — secretary for correspondence

    also used · classical · Suet. Claud. 28: Narcissum ab epistulīs (Lewis & Short, s.v. ab); Traupman 375: corresponding secretary; Traupman 297

    The title of the imperial secretary for letters; for a secretary who keeps the minutes, see scrība.

  • sēcrētārius, sēcrētāriī m. — a secretary

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 375: sēcrētārius (-a, f.)

    Traupman’s word, after the modern languages; it is not in Lewis & Short. For a government secretary of state, see minister.

Examples

  • notārium vocō et quae fōrmāverim dictō

    I call my secretary and dictate what I have composedPlin. Ep. 9.36.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • Epistulam librāriō dictāvī; crās mittētur.

    I dictated the letter to my secretary; it will go tomorrow.composed

See also minister, employee, office.
